local_checks.invariant: Credentials, emails and answer/draft text never reach a log sink with a broader reader than the device owner.
local_checks.result: Log._emit (log.dart:94-115) redacts message and fields (key regex redact.dart:9-12 covers token/session/email/answer/draft; value regexes :14-23 cover JWT, bearer, email, Supabase secret). The only sink is developerSink -> dart:developer (log.dart:40-48); no remote sink (Sentry/PostHog) is wired anywhere in lib (only Env fields exist, env.dart:15-40). All call sites log runtimeType or enum codes, never rows. No lower-trust reader of logs exists in source. local_checks.invariant: After sign-out, the previous player's local data (DB, prefs, cached AI scores, leaderboard cache, resume slots) does not surface under the next guest.

_hardening: apps/mobile/lib/core/logging/log.dart:45 forwards the raw, unredacted error object (and stack) to developer.log. Only fields/message/toJson error are redacted. It is local-only today, but would leak if a remote sink (Sentry, planned) reused LogRecord.error.

AndroidManifest.xml <application> sets no android:allowBackup/dataExtractionRules, so the drift DB (attempts incl. drafts) and the Supabase session in SharedPreferences are included in the user's own cloud backup / device transfer. Same principal, so not a finding; consider excluding the session store.
PlayerData.clear uses SQL DELETE without VACUUM/secure_delete, so freed SQLite pages may retain the previous player's drafts on disk until overwritten (same-device forensic residue only).

release-apk.yml (contents: write) uses mutable action tags (actions/checkout@v4, setup-java@v4, subosito/flutter-action@v2, upload-artifact@v4) and flutter-action cache:true. Pin actions to commit SHAs. A dispatch can also --clobber assets on an existing (even published) release for any tag and --target any branch SHA; both are writer-only.

The web static export defines no CSP, X-Frame-Options or Referrer-Policy (next.config.ts, no vercel.json). There is no state-changing action, so this is hardening only. /verified strips code/error from the URL via replaceState, but a ?code= from the PKCE email-change redirect is still sent to Vercel in the request line/logs (not exchangeable without the device's verifier).

local_checks.invariant: claim_ai_score counts atomically per (uid, UTC day) with a server-held limit; no race, overflow or client-raisable limit
local_checks.result: Single INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE used < 30 (lines 95-100) is atomic per row; limit is a constant in SQL (line 88); day comes from server now() in UTC (line 96); ai_score_usage has no write grant (lines 76-77). Within one uid the counter holds. The accounting dimension is the uid, which anonymous sign-in mints for free (config.toml 188, 213), so per-person spend is bounded only by the hosted anonymous sign-in rate limit.

local_checks.invariant: one quota unit buys a bounded amount of Gemini work, weighted for cost
local_checks.result: The quota is claimed once (score handler.ts:72, voice handler.ts:82) before Gemini, so failures still count. But scoreWithFallback / scoreVoiceWithFallback try up to 3 models per claim on any UpstreamError/OutputError including timeout (gemini.ts:153-159, gemini_voice.ts:121-129), and the voice path sends up to 2x4 MB audio per call (voice.ts:68) while costing the same single unit as a text score. A ~3x amplification per unit, bounded.

local_checks.invariant: request bodies are size-capped before buffering and before caller identity is validated
local_checks.result: score: handler.ts:63 calls req.json() with no size cap at all; per-field caps (scoring.ts:57-66) apply only after the whole body is buffered and parsed. score-voice: handler.ts:65 trusts content-length (absent header => 0 passes), then handler.ts:73 req.text() buffers the full body before the raw.length check at :74. Both happen after only a presence check of a Bearer string (handler.ts:47-59) and before the first JWT validation (PostgREST in claimQuota). Whether the platform gateway (verify_jwt, request-size limit) blocks this first is a deployment fact.

local_checks.invariant: Composite-key collision: the globally unique client-supplied mission_attempts.attempt_id (PK, upsert on conflict do nothing) cannot be used by one player to pre-empt or overwrite another player's attempt
local_checks.result: attempt_id is a global PK without user_id (create_mission_attempts.sql:9), so a pre-inserted id would silently drop a victim's later sync; however ids are v4 UUIDs from Random.secure() (ids.dart:5-12, drift_progress_repository.dart:26) and are never exposed to other players (the leaderboard returns no ids), so an attacker cannot learn or guess a victim's id.
